name: colAvgsPerRowSet
title: Applies a column-by-column averaging function to equally-sized subsets of matrix rows

origin.description: Applies a column-by-column averaging function to equally-sized subsets of matrix rows. Each subset is averaged independently of the others.
origin.usage:
colAvgsPerRowSet(X, W = NULL, cols = NULL, S, FUN = colMeans, ...,
  na.rm = NA, tFUN = FALSE)

arguments.name: X
arguments.text: A numeric N by M matrix.

arguments.name: W
arguments.text: An optional numeric N by M matrix of weights.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: S
arguments.text: An integer K by J matrix specifying the J subsets. Each column holds K row indexes for the corresponding subset.

arguments.name: FUN
arguments.text: The column-by-column function used to average over each subset of X. This function must accept a numeric K by M matrix and the logical argument na.rm, and return a numeric vector of length M.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: Logical argument passed to FUN as na.rm. If NA, which is the default, then na.rm = TRUE is used if X or S holds missing values, otherwise na.rm = FALSE.

arguments.name: tFUN
arguments.text: If TRUE, the matrix passed to FUN is transposed first. The implementation flips this flag before calling rowAvgsPerColSet.

origin.details: The matrix is transposed and passed to rowAvgsPerColSet, with tFUN flipped, and the result is transposed back. If S is a single column vector with indices 1:N, colAvgsPerRowSet(X, S = S, FUN = colMeans) gives the same result as colMeans(X).
origin.value: A numeric J by M matrix. Row names come from colnames(S) and column names come from X. One row is one row-set.

translation.description: Applies a column-by-column averaging function to equally-sized subsets of matrix rows. Each subset is averaged independently of the others.
translation.usage:
colAvgsPerRowSet(X, W=None, cols=None, S=None, FUN=None, na_rm=None,
  t_fun=False, **kwargs)

arguments.name: X
arguments.text: A 2-d numeric array. Axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns, matching the printed R matrix.

arguments.name: W
arguments.text: An optional numeric array with the same shape as X. cols subsets X. A matrix W is not subset by cols, so the shapes then disagree.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A base-R column subscript, 1-based when numeric. None keeps every column.

arguments.name: S
arguments.text: A 2-d array of 1-based row indexes. Each column is one set. Non-finite indexes are dropped inside rowAvgsPerColSet.

arguments.name: FUN
arguments.text: Callable applied after the transpose. None uses the base column-means rule. It is passed through with t_fun flipped.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: Passed through to rowAvgsPerColSet. None matches R's NA rule on the transposed matrix and on S.

arguments.name: t_fun
arguments.text: When False, which is the default, the transposed column subset is transposed again before FUN. This is tFUN, flipped on the way in.

translation.details: colAvgsPerRowSet transposes X and W, calls rowAvgsPerColSet with the flipped t_fun, and transposes the result. The default call matches column means of each selected row set. The result is a plain array. Names are not attached.
translation.value: A numeric array of shape (number of sets, selected columns).
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowavgs import colAvgsPerRowSet

colAvgsPerRowSet(np.array([[1, 3, 5], [2, 4, 6]], dtype=float), S=np.array([[1], [2]]))
